issues.legal_issue: The suit for recovery of income from property held for a religious endowment was maintainable against the challenge raised.
material_facts: The deity sued through a sole trustee appointed by the religious endowment board to recover arrears of income and obtain a direction for future payment.
The defendants challenged the maintainability of the suit, but the Supreme Court was not shown how the suit was not maintainable.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to maintainability was rejected because no basis for it had been shown.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated no separate legal test for maintainability; it rejected the objection because the appellants had not shown how the suit was not maintainable.

predicates.suit_seeks_recovery_for_religious_endowm: A religious endowment, acting through its trustee, brought a suit to recover income or obtain payment for its purposes.
predicates.maintainability_objection_unsubstantiate: The defendants challenged the suit's maintainability but did not show a basis for finding the suit not maintainable.

issues.definition: When a religious endowment sues through its trustee to recover income or obtain payment for its purposes and the defendants do not substantiate a maintainability objection, the objection is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be amended to add a formal prayer for relief when the necessary allegations and evidence are already before the court and the amendment does not change the cause of action or require a new trial.
material_facts: The original plaint sought recovery of arrears and future payments for services and expenses associated with the deity.
The proposed amendment added a declaration that the properties and their income formed a specific endowment and that the defendants were liable to pay the entire income.
The necessary allegations had been made, an issue had been framed on the nature of the grant, the parties knew the dispute, and the relevant evidence had been adduced.
The High Court considered the added prayer formal and found it introduced neither a new cause of action nor a need for a fresh trial.
issues.conclusion: The High Court rightly allowed the amendment adding the declaratory prayer.
issues.legal_principle: An amendment adding a formal relief may be allowed where the relevant allegations and evidence are already present, the parties have addressed the real controversy, and the amendment neither changes the cause of action nor requires a fresh trial. The Court relied on no earlier case or statutory provision for this conclusion.

rule.if: civil_appeal_reviews_pleading_amendment and necessary_allegations_already_pleaded and parties_understood_real_dispute and relevant_evidence_already_led and amendment_adds_formal_relief and not amendment_changes_cause_of_action and not amendment_requires_fresh_trial

predicates.civil_appeal_reviews_pleading_amendment: The matter is a civil appeal in which the court reviews an order allowing an amendment to a pleading.
predicates.necessary_allegations_already_pleaded: The original pleading already contains the allegations needed to support the proposed relief.
predicates.parties_understood_real_dispute: The parties knew the real controversy and had addressed it in the proceedings.
predicates.relevant_evidence_already_led: The parties had already adduced the evidence relevant to the controversy.
predicates.amendment_adds_formal_relief: The amendment adds a prayer for relief flowing from the existing allegations.
predicates.amendment_changes_cause_of_action: The amendment changes the cause of action.
predicates.amendment_requires_fresh_trial: The amendment requires a fresh trial.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal reviewing a pleading amendment, the amendment is allowed when the necessary allegations, understanding of the dispute, and relevant evidence are already present, and the added formal relief changes neither the cause of action nor the need for a fresh trial.

issues.legal_issue: A grant shown by the records and admissions to have been made for a deity's specified religious service is a specific endowment rather than a personal grant burdened by a service obligation.
material_facts: An inam statement recorded that the land and its income were for the deity's Kalyanotsavam and that the income had been used to perform it.

The inam register classified the grant as a religious endowment, described service in the temple, and recorded that the service was performed and the grant was to continue so long as the service was performed.
The register did not say that the grant was confirmed to an individual so long as that individual performed the service.
The grant's title deed and sanad were not produced, but predecessors of the defendants had admitted that they were trustees of the Kalyanotsavam and had performed the service.
Both lower courts found that the lands were endowed for the Kalyanotsavam and incidental purposes.
issues.conclusion: The grant was a specific endowment for the deity's Kalyanotsavam and incidental purposes, not a personal grant burdened with an obligation to perform the service.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated inam registers as evidence of utmost importance and read the records together with the admissions. It applied the distinction discussed in Hindu Religious Endowments, Madras v. Thadikonda Koteswara Rao, AIR 1937 Mad. 852: language continuing a grant so long as service is performed does not itself establish a personal grant, unlike language confirming the grant to a person so long as that person performs the service.

rule.if: civil_appeal_reviews_endowment_classification and records_identify_religious_purpose and income_used_for_specified_service and register_does_not_confirm_grant_to_individual and predecessor_admissions_support_trustee_role

predicates.civil_appeal_reviews_endowment_classific: The matter is a civil appeal reviewing whether a grant is a religious endowment or a personal grant.
predicates.records_identify_religious_purpose: The grant records identify a specified religious purpose for the property or its income.
predicates.income_used_for_specified_service: The evidence shows that income from the property was used to perform the specified religious service.
predicates.register_does_not_confirm_grant_to_indiv: The register does not state that the grant was confirmed to an individual for as long as that individual performed the service.
predicates.predecessor_admissions_support_trustee_r: The grant holders' predecessors admitted that they acted as trustees and performed the specified religious service.

issues.definition: A grant is a specific endowment when, in an appeal about its classification, the records identify a religious purpose, the income was used for that purpose, the register does not confirm the grant to an individual, and predecessor admissions support a trustee role.

issues.legal_issue: When the whole income of property was originally devoted to a specific charitable or religious purpose, a later increase in income remains devoted to that purpose, and surplus that cannot be spent on the specified service may be applied cy-près.
material_facts: The grant's original annual income was Rs. 11, and the evidence supported the finding that the whole amount was spent on the deity's Kalyanotsavam.
The property's value and income later increased beyond the expenditure required for that particular service.
The High Court held that the whole income was for the deity and applied the cy-près doctrine to any surplus that could not be spent on the specified service.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in holding that the whole income was to go to the deity, including any surplus dealt with under the cy-près doctrine.
issues.legal_principle: The Court inferred from the original income being exhausted by the charitable purpose that the intention was to devote the whole income to charity, so later increases accrued to the charity. It relied on Hindu Religious Endowments v. Thadikonda Koteswara Rao, AIR 1937 Mad. 852; Tudor on Charities (5th ed.), p. 164; and Laws of England, vol. 4, para. 624, p. 303. It also applied the cy-près principle for surplus from a specific endowment that cannot be spent on the specified services, relying on N. Sankaranarayana Pillayan v. Board of Commissioners for Hindu Religious Endowments, Madras, (1947) L.R. 74 I.A. 230.

predicates.civil_appeal_reviews_income_of_specific_: The matter is a civil appeal about the use of income from a specific endowment.
predicates.original_income_fully_devoted_to_purpose: The whole of the property's original income was devoted to the charitable or religious purpose for which it was granted.
predicates.later_income_exceeds_cost_of_specified_s: The property's later income exceeds what is needed for the specified service.
predicates.surplus_cannot_be_spent_on_specified_ser: The surplus cannot be spent on the specified service.

issues.definition: When the original income of a specific endowment was fully devoted to its purpose and later income exceeds the cost of the specified service, any unspendable surplus does not take the income outside the charitable purpose.
